 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Troy Aikman's radio appearance on Thursday, Nov. 19, came with a little side serving of a snide shot at Joe Buck.
 With co-host Craig Miller out sick, Aikman noted that host George Dunham was "flying solo today," and when Dunham asked whether he wanted to come in and just hang out, Aikman answered with a line about his Monday Night Football partner at ESPN.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "Joe's always wanted a one-man booth," he said, before turning it back on Dunham with, "I'm wondering if you've always wanted a one-man radio show," as his host chuckled.
 As Aikman added fuel to the fire amid reports of his rift with Buck, there was a school of thought that ESPN could step in and take action after his latest remarks, potentially even pull him from the booth for its Super Bowl broadcast. However, former ESPN host Bomani Jones isn't convinced ESPN could just pull Aikman off the call.
 Bomani Jones Brings the NFL Into ESPN's Troy Aikman Question
 Jones framed his take around why ESPN hired the pair in the first place.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "They hired Buck and Aikman to trade on their credibility to land a Super Bowl. Which is to say, we sure the NFL is gonna be cool with pulling Aikman? It's just gonna have to be weird, I reckon."
 Jones posed it as a question of his own, and it lands with ESPN set to broadcast its first Super Bowl this season, Aikman still unsigned, and both men sharing the booth on Monday nights.
 How Joe Buck's Partnership With Aikman Reached This Point
 Contracts hang over all of it. Buck signed a six-year extension in September that the New York Post reported is worth $108 million, while Aikman is still without a new deal.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Things came to a head before the Oct. 12 Bills-Rams game in Week 5, when the two reportedly had an on-field confrontation before calling Buffalo's 37-34 overtime win at SoFi Stadium.
 Asked about reports of the argument on Oct. 15, Aikman didn't deny them, saying, "There's probably a time and a place for all that. I don't know if now is the time. I don't know if it's hard to figure out kind of what happened."
 PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN's Free NFL Playoff Predictor 
 He was far more direct about where he is headed. "I'll broadcast through this season and I'll be a free agent at the end of the year and kind of see what happens. I'm looking forward to whatever the rest of this season does hold and the Super Bowl and all that and where my next landing spot may be."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Two weeks later, former New York Post reporter Andrew Marchand reported that the exchange was laced with profanity, with Buck asking Aikman, "You are not going to [expletive] talk to me?" and telling him, "I'm not the reason you don't have a contract."
 The noise reached the top of the network this week. ESPN chief Jimmy Pitaro said Tuesday, two days before Aikman's radio line, that the media coverage of the Buck and Aikman situation has been "disappointing."
 What Comes Next for the Monday Night Football Booth
 The next Monday night game on the schedule sends the Cincinnati Bengals to face the Washington Commanders on Nov. 23 at 8:15 p.m. ET.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement From there, the schedule runs through the rest of the regular season to ESPN's first Super Bowl, after which Aikman expects to be a free agent.
